candidate.name: Ethosuximide (T-type calcium-channel blocker class contrast; lead DL-MECH-170)

disease_assertion.endpoint: PTZ-provoked behavioural seizure score, late phase of the hour (graphical reading)
disease_assertion.source: Cheng 2020, Figure 7b, as re-read in the R2 note (section 9)
disease_assertion.locator: R2 note repurposing_10h_scientist-b_20261021.md section 9, point 2: the null arm has a sustained late phase that the wild type does not

context.developmental_stage: preweaning mouse (as the R2 note describes the Wwox PTZ assay; the exact age is not carried)

disease_assertion.note: Graphical reading from a moderate-resolution time course, N = 6 in the null arm. The R2 note twice describes this assay as a preweaning mouse; the exact age is not carried.

drug_assertions.endpoint: PTZ-provoked behavioural seizure score, late phase of the hour (graphical reading)
drug_assertions.source: Cheng 2020 Figure 7b (WWOX-direct, one laboratory), restated by the R2 note
drug_assertions.locator: deepdive_manifests/PMID32000863.json: «Pretreatment of an antiepileptic drug ethosuximide suppressed PTZ-induced seizure in Wwox−/− mice (Fig. 7b), although ethosuximide pretreatment had no effects on the behavior changes in Wwox+/+ and Wwox+/− mice treated with a low dose of PTZ.»
drug_assertions.note: R2 reading: the effect is confined to the second half of the hour, the PTZ-alone null control varies between the ethosuximide and the lithium experiments by a comparable order to the late effect (the Methods do not say whether the cohorts are separate), and the paper reports per-genotype brackets with no drug-by-genotype interaction test.

drug_assertions.endpoint: PTZ-provoked behavioural seizure score, late phase of the hour (graphical reading)
drug_assertions.source: Cheng 2020 Figure 7b, restated by the R2 note (section 9, point 1)
drug_assertions.locator: R2 note section 9: the wild-type ethosuximide curve crosses the PTZ-alone curve instead of separating; the wild type has no late phase to suppress
drug_assertions.note: Neither a protective effect nor a clear absence. Whether the contrast is a floor effect, a baseline effect or a real null-specific effect is not distinguished by these data.

drug_assertions.endpoint: viability of embryonic cortical progenitors in vitro
drug_assertions.source: Kim 2018 as read in the R2 note section 7 (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
drug_assertions.locator: R2 note section 7: two research T-type blockers lowered viability and phospho-AKT and phospho-GSK3 beta; ethosuximide was not tested
drug_assertions.note: Hypothesis-generating class-level safety signal only: in vitro, research compounds, Cav3.1-dependent; in vivo and clinical significance unknown; not an administration statement and not a statement about ethosuximide.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: late-phase PTZ-provoked behavioural seizure score in a three-genotype design with an explicit drug-by-genotype interaction test and a concurrent same-day PTZ-alone control (the falsifier of DL-MECH-170); no human endpoint is yet defined for this candidate
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: one mouse experiment, one laboratory, symptomatic class; no T-type current measured in any Wwox system; one bulk RNA-seq supplementary table of an adult P47T knock-in hippocampus lists Cacna1g up (log2 +1.22) and Cacna1h down (log2 -1.02), mRNA level only, a different region, composition effect not excluded (R2 section 28); no human T-type evidence in WWOX
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: acute pretreatment (route not carried), constitutive null genotype only, provoked behavioural endpoint, graphical effect confined to the late phase; no missense or compound-heterozygous genotype; no spontaneous-seizure or EEG endpoint

cellular_context.target_expression: UNKNOWN for current and protein: no T-type current measured in any Wwox system (R2 section 13); at mRNA level Cacna1g is up and Cacna1h down in adult P47T knock-in hippocampus (R2 section 28), which is neither thalamus, nor a null, nor preweaning
cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: UNKNOWN; whole-animal behavioural endpoint; in ethosuximide-sensitive models the T-type current is reduced in relay (GAERS, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE) or reticular neurons, so its sign is per lesion
cellular_context.coverage: partial: mRNA only, one region, one adult knock-in; no current, protein or thalamic measurement
cellular_context.limits: target expression is not drug selectivity or exposure; a channel's contribution to excitability differs between immature and mature neurons of one structure (R2 section 14), so an age-blind reading of 'T-type block lowers excitability' is unsafe

p4_roadmap_fields.identity: Ethosuximide, an approved antiseizure drug; the class contrast is T-type calcium-channel block. Formulation not carried; no dose, route or schedule.
p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Origin: the Wwox-null mouse PTZ experiment (WWOX-direct), not another disease. Transfer to human WOREE: untested; one experiment, one laboratory, symptomatic class at best.
p4_roadmap_fields.novelty_for_woree: Not found in the research (dated queries 2026-10-21, R2 note section 13): no abstract-indexed paper for WWOX with ethosuximide, and one hit for WWOX with T-type terms that holds gene counts only. By dismissal-ledger D-37 this licenses 'no abstract-indexed paper', not 'never measured': the one Wwox ethosuximide assay sits inside a paper whose abstract lacks the term.
p4_roadmap_fields.known_roads_state: Partial (known-roads note 2.3), now narrowed by the R2 note: not a clean genotype-specific effect. The lithium arm of the same figure suppressed in all three genotypes (relevant negative on specificity).
p4_roadmap_fields.path_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE (symptomatic class). The lead would become a mechanism to test only if the falsifier survives; it is not a RECUPERO_PROFONDO candidate.
p4_roadmap_fields.expected_contribution: Symptom (provoked seizure). Not disease modification: in a digenic absence mouse (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE) the ethosuximide effect and a Cav3.1 deletion suppressed the seizure and left a quantified comorbidity untouched (R2 section 6).
p4_roadmap_fields.mechanism: Premise: T-type block pulls back an excess created by loss of WWOX. UNKNOWN in WWOX. Non-T-type routes reported for ethosuximide in non-WWOX systems: GIRK block, a reticular-nucleus site, broad cortical effects, a FOXO-pathway effect in worms; none shown in a Wwox system. T-type excess is a recognised cause of disease in humans (gain-of-function variants in the T-type channel genes) but is not shown in a WWOX null. Candidate extra read-out proposed by R2: phospho-Ser9 GSK3 beta in any Wwox-null ethosuximide experiment (an IPOTESI from two non-matching systems).
p4_roadmap_fields.sources: Internal, WWOX: DL-MECH-170, CLAIM 016 and its lithium boundary note, Cheng 2020 manifest, FT-115. R2 note (scientist-b), landed on main (integration commit 190b389e; closure commit 743f9914 records three blind audits, among them the Cheng 2020 locators 6 of 6 SUPPORTED with soft corrections, and wording repairs that are themselves unaudited); its narrowing of DL-MECH-170 remains owed a blind audit by someone else. Adjacent, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: the R2 papers (Gnb1, Gabrb3, Hcn1, Cntnap2, Grin2b, digenic absence, worm and relay-neuron strain studies).
p4_roadmap_fields.evidence_pro_contra: Pro: in one three-genotype experiment ethosuximide's effect was marked significant in the null panel only. Contra: late-phase restriction; cohort variability of a comparable order to the effect; the wild-type baseline is small but not zero, and lithium was still detected inside the same low range (so a pure floor effect is not established); no interaction test; Gnb1 mouse shows the default outcome of a mutant-only effect when the wild-type baseline is near zero; mechanism may be non-T-type; GAERS has less T-type current than its control.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Not assessed in any record read. Clinical census 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven unfiltered queries on ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the one WOREE record is an observational registry and natural-history study. Its own caution binds this card: «A missing hit does not prove that no study exists.» An NCT number proves neither recruitment nor first dosing. FT-115 (no patient-level T-type evidence) was confirmed at full-text depth for four documents (R2 section 13) and is not retired as a statement about the literature.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_benefit: UNKNOWN. No human age-at-treatment datum of any kind exists; no experiment in any WWOX model varies age at treatment beyond mouse P5 (early-benefit note, section 4).
p4_roadmap_fields.pharmacology: UNKNOWN for a Wwox system. The R2 note carries, from papers it read, that ethosuximide's own T-type potency is in the millimolar range and disputed at relevant concentrations; exposure and CNS exposure in WOREE: UNKNOWN.
p4_roadmap_fields.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. Class-level signal only: T-type blockers reduce progenitor viability in vitro (research compounds, rat, Cav3.1-dependent), significance unknown. In a DEE mouse model (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE) some antiseizure drug classes aggravated spiking, so 'an antiseizure drug suppresses in the mutant' is not a safe default and a falsifier needs a harm arm. Suitability not presumed.
p4_roadmap_fields.verification_scope: Supported by: one experiment (Cheng 2020). R2 re-read depth: partial. The R2 note has landed and three of its readings were blind-audited at its closure; the narrowing of the lead and of the CLAIM 016 framing, and the wording repairs, are unaudited: blind audit OWED. This card was blind-audited on 2026-10-22 (the sections this version repairs are unaudited).
p4_roadmap_fields.question_history: DL-MECH-170 (open), CLAIM 016, FT-115, known-roads note 2.3, R2 note.
p4_roadmap_fields.next_measure: Is the late-phase ethosuximide effect in the null reproduced, with a drug-by-genotype interaction test, a concurrent same-day PTZ-alone control in every cell and a per-genotype baseline stated? The R2 design sketch says power depends mainly on which control cohort is representative, not on N alone.
p4_roadmap_fields.status: IPOTESI (open lead; the R2 note has landed, its narrowing and wording repairs are unaudited).
p4_roadmap_fields.value_added: Replaces 'the drug the paper did not favour behaved genotype-specifically' with the time-resolved reading, the cohort-variability problem, the non-T-type mechanisms and a class-level developmental safety line.

not_known: exact mouse age in the experiment (preweaning per the R2 note)
any T-type current or protein measurement in a Wwox system (an mRNA observation exists, R2 section 28)

evaluation_frame.source: repurposing_10h_scientist-d_20261021.md, 'The answer in one page', DESIGN TABLE A and B. INFERENZA built from precedents that are all NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; the manifests of that note were blind-audited on 2026-10-22 (207 of 215 triples supported, eight repaired; the repairs are unaudited).
a_woree_evaluation_would_have_to_measure: a repeated, instrument-matched baseline before any exposure, in a form that can move in a profoundly impaired child (growth-scale or raw-score forms rather than standard scores); no measurement of the scatter of an untreated interval in WOREE is established here (the repository's series have one timepoint per patient; no wider search was run)
a pharmacodynamic anchor: none exists for any WWOX-directed intervention (CLAIM 046), so engagement of the intended target cannot be shown at all
one prespecified endpoint with a rescue or withdrawal rule written before the observation window opens
survival, reported beside whatever endpoint is chosen
seizures only as a separate, declared family: a countable fraction, a diary or agreed reconstruction rule, and the seizure-free stratum reported apart (it is prognostic, not a treatment effect)
and_could_not_claim: disease modification or developmental benefit: the developmental-delay row of the one WOREE series reporting a response is identical in every column and two of the three responders had died
that seizure control protects development (CLAIM 031 forbids counting any symptomatic outcome as disease modification)
benefit from a pharmacodynamic move, a global impression or an own-baseline comparison
any effect smaller than the instrument's own untreated scatter

the word protection: in the human precedents read for this frame none measured the preservation of a function that would otherwise have been lost; the repository's mouse rescue studies are outside this frame and the scope of 'this corpus' is not defined, so no wider negative is established here

must_never: No score, rank, probability or blended index. 'Non-dominated' would be a statement about visible dimensions, never a number.
No dose, route, schedule, course or paediatric suitability. Accessibility of a drug, diet or supplement does not prove paediatric suitability.
A computational prediction is not DATO. No engine was run for this card.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE and is never promoted to WWOX evidence.
A missing hit is not proof of absence.
Symptomatic benefit is not slowing of disease; the word 'protection' is not licensed by any evidence on this card.
Where CLAIM 011 has been narrowed, 'dose-dependent' does not stand.
Nothing here is medical advice; it supports discussion with a treating clinical team and never substitutes for one.
